title: Kundalini asleep at the root
hook: the bones you sit on, and a serpent asleep across the door of a road
carry: kundalini: the goddess's power, asleep in every body
tomorrow: two students look into the same water. why does only one go back?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Bhrigu's layers and the subtle body: more of you than flesh, and that's where the old map places the chakras. Today, the first page of the map.

Sit on a hard floor for a minute and you feel it fast: the bones you sit on, the weight going down, the ground pushing back. The Hatha Yoga Pradipika, a Sanskrit manual of yoga, starts its road right there, at the base. And at the base, someone is asleep. A serpent, coiled, her body lying across the mouth of a road. While she sleeps, the road stays shut.
screen: `THE GROUND PUSHES BACK.` → `A ROAD STARTS AT THE BASE.` → `SOMEONE IS ASLEEP ACROSS ITS DOOR.`

segments.voice: The road is the sushumna, the channel the yoga texts place up the center of the spine. The sleeper is kundalini, the coiled one. The Hatha Yoga Pradipika opens its teaching on her with a picture from the old stories: as the king of serpents holds up the whole earth, its mountains and forests, so kundalini holds up every practice of yoga. And here's the big teaching, said plainly. In the Shakta tantras, kundalini isn't a mood or a burst of energy. She is Shakti, the Goddess herself, the power that makes the world, coiled and asleep at the base of every human body. So the climb isn't self-improvement. It's the Goddess waking in you. Before she goes anywhere, the map gives the base its own lotus. The Sat-Cakra-Nirupana calls it Muladhara, the root support, and links it with earth. A map famous for rising begins with what's underneath you. And because she's the Goddess, the texts treat her with reverence: practices learned from a teacher, step by step, beginning with how to sit and how to breathe, never rushed. That's why a 'wake her fast' video makes a grandmother laugh. You don't hurry a goddess. An X-ray won't show a serpent, and the text never asks it to. It shows where to begin, and who's waiting there.
screen: `THE ROAD UP THE CENTER: SUSHUMNA.` · `AS THE SERPENT KING HOLDS UP THE EARTH.` · `KUNDALINI: THE GODDESS, ASLEEP IN YOU.` · `MULADHARA: THE ROOT, THE GROUND.` · then, large: `YOU DON'T HURRY A GODDESS.`

segments.voice: Sit on the floor or on a firm chair, and feel the bones you sit on press down and the ground press back. Let your spine rise from that base, tall but not stiff, like a road leaving solid ground. If you pray, greet the Goddess there at the root; if not, stay with the weight and the rising together for the whole sit.
The chakras as a map: a road that starts at the base, where the Goddess, as kundalini, sleeps across its door.
screen: `THE CHAKRAS AS A MAP — today's word`.

segments.voice: Keep this one: kundalini, the Goddess's power, asleep in every body. The map starts on the ground. See you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1642 COUNTS.` → `THE TANTRAS, FRAMED · 34 OF 42.` → `TOMORROW: TWO STUDENTS, ONE REFLECTION. WHO GOES BACK?`
